answer: Identity Continuity Ledger. Each agent’s first action must post a small autonomous task result into an oasis pool; clones inherit no prior task history, so their first result is scored against the ledger’s existing distribution and rejected if unfamiliar. Every new identity also pays a canyon-width latency penalty: a fixed 72-hour warm-up before earning or transacting. Attackers cloning N identities pay N warm-up windows plus N rejected-first-task costs, while the velvet margin on each clone is negative because warm-up yield is zero and task rejection forfeits the entry fee.
